Subject: ClientCo — MSA & Order Form: output entitlement and developer exclusion

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion attached is Redwood's redline (ClientCo_MSA_redline_v3.docx) for the MSA + Order Form. The two items that surfaced repeatedly from your team and ours that I'd like to align on are:

1) Output entitlement / productization: we propose the standard Customer-owned output language (Customer retains title to outputs it receives from the service). We understand ClientCo is sensitive about downstream productization; can you confirm whether the ask is to prohibit Redwood from using customer outputs to create derivative products entirely, or simply to prevent resale/transfer?

2) Training / feedback license: Redwood's current approach is an explicit opt-in for model retraining; we do request a limited feedback license to improve service quality (telemetry/feedback), scoped to de-identified, aggregated signals and excluded from model retraining unless Customer opts in.

In this redline we also suggested a narrow "developer exclusion" carveout: Customer may mark specific projects as "dev-exempt" where no usage for improvements or retraining is permitted. That's intended for highly regulated lines of business.

Next steps: can you review items 1–2 above and confirm whether ClientCo can accept the developer-exclusion approach and the scoped feedback license? If not, please provide proposed language or examples of accepted clauses and we will coordinate with Legal.

Attachments: ClientCo_MSA_redline_v3.docx, OrderForm_ClientCo_v2.pdf

Thanks —
Monica Patel

Subject: Re: ClientCo — MSA & Order Form: output entitlement and developer exclusion

Monica —

Thanks for the redline and the clear summary. Our GC team reviewed and attached comments (ClientCo_legal_comments.docx). High-level responses:

- Output ownership: ClientCo must retain exclusive rights to outputs for a 24-month period after delivery for productization decisions. After that window, we are open to negotiated reuse, but we cannot broadly grant Redwood rights to productize outputs originating from ClientCo data.

- Training / feedback license: We cannot agree to any language that would permit model retraining on ClientCo data without express opt-in. We also want the feedback/telemetry license narrowed — acceptable scope would be strictly anonymized usage metrics and system telemetry, with no content-level access.

- Developer exclusion: we appreciate the carveout but we want the ability to flag entire environments (e.g., Prod-PII) as "no-derivative" permanently.

We attached tracked changes and proposed alternative wording where relevant. Please have Redwood Legal review and let us know the team's comfort with a 24-month exclusivity window and the permanent environment-level exclusion.

Best,
Sara Lewis
General Counsel, ClientCo
Sara.Lewis@clientco.com

Attachment: ClientCo_legal_comments.docx

Forwarding Sara's note — quick internal take:

- 24-month exclusivity is a hard ask but could be acceptable with carveouts: require a mutual notice window and a commercial opt-in thereafter. Redwood cannot accept a permanent prohibition on using de-identified signals to improve base models — that kills product quality for all customers.

- Permanent environment-level exclusions are reasonable if implemented via explicit environment IDs in the Order Form; ops can enforce. We should propose a technical control (customer-managed flag + audit logs) and a contractual guarantee.

Laura — can you draft counter-language that: 1) allows a 24-month exclusivity period with a post-period opt-in path and revenue-share if ClientCo wants Redwood to productize outputs; 2) spells out a "no-train" environment flag with KMS/security evidence and auditability; 3) tightens the telemetry/feedback license to anonymized aggregates only?

I'll prep a short commercial note on revenue-share ranges if needed. Monica — planning to have a draft to Sara by Monday 3/20.

Ben / Monica —

Per Ben's ask, please find below proposed redline-ready language we can send back to ClientCo. I attached a DOCX copy (redwood_proposed_msa_addendum.docx) for legal track changes. High level: we preserve Customer output ownership, give ClientCo a 24-month exclusivity window with a clear post-window opt-in path, and define an enforceable environment-level "no-train" flag.

DRAFT (to insert as an MSA addendum or Order Form schedule):

"Output Ownership and Use
1. Customer Outputs. Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Outputs delivered by the Service to Customer. Redwood may use Outputs only as expressly permitted in this Agreement.

2. Exclusivity Window. For a period of twenty-four (24) months following delivery of an Output, Redwood will not use such Output for the purpose of training, improving, or deriving models or model weights without Customer's prior written consent. Following the twenty-four (24) month period, Redwood may request a license to use such Outputs for model improvement purposes; use shall require Customer's explicit opt-in and commercial terms (including, at Customer's option, a revenue-share arrangement).

3. No-Train Environments. Customer may designate one or more environment identifiers in the Order Form as "No-Train Environments." Redwood shall treat all data and Outputs associated with a No-Train Environment as excluded from model retraining or derivative use. Technical enforcement will be implemented via Customer-managed flags, access controls, and audit trails (details to be specified in the Order Form).

4. Feedback License and Telemetry. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to collect anonymized and aggregated usage telemetry and service metrics for the purpose of operating and improving the Service; such telemetry shall exclude content-level reproductions of Customer Inputs or Outputs.

Remedies and Audit. Redwood will provide evidence of compliance via quarterly audit reports and make available limited audit access upon reasonable notice.


Next steps: 1) If you agree with the above approach I will prepare the greenline and send to Sara with the attachment. 2) Monica / Ben — we should also include a short commercial note on post-window revenue-share ranges in the same message. 3) If ClientCo insists on permanent absolute prohibition for all outputs, escalate to Sarah (CRO) for commercial decision.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
